Subject: Finex - post-call: throughput & SLOs

Thanks for the call today, Rafael — good conversation. Quick recap and the items we need from you to size this properly: 

Summary of Finex requirements (from product & infra):
- Use case: customer support chat + doc Q&A (hybrid). Majority of calls are short multi-turn chat (avg 3 turns).
- Steady-state QPS: ~200 requests/sec (long-running average).
- Peak QPS: ~1,200 requests/sec (bursts, ~5–10 minutes, ~4 bursts/day expected).
- Tokens per request: avg 300 tokens (prompt + response). Max 1,024 token context, but typical <512.
- Concurrency requirement: support 500 concurrent open sessions (streaming for UX).
- Latency targets: P50 <= 250 ms (generation latency for short responses), P95 <= 500 ms, P99 <= 800 ms.
- Streaming: required — client needs token-by-token delivery for chat.
- Availability/SLO: 99.9% regional uptime, regional fallback acceptable.

Open questions for you:
1) What throughput sizing (tokens/sec, GPU counts) would you recommend for steady vs peak?
2) How do you handle streaming + batching tradeoffs (to hit P99 targets while batching for cost)?
3) Any initial config suggestion (quantization, instance types, concurrency per GPU) and estimate of cost for hosted vs dedicated?

We can share traffic samples and a short snapshot of concurrency distribution — attaching the sample inputs (finex-sizing-inputs.xlsx).

Next steps: please send an initial sizing + recommended config and I'll set up a call with our infra lead if we need deeper perf testing.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, Finex Capital

Attachment: finex-sizing-inputs.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Finex - post-call: throughput & SLOs

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the sizing inputs. This is helpful. High-level responses below; I attached our initial suggested config and a short playbook (redwood-initial-suggested-config.pdf) so you can see the assumptions.

Quick answers / assumptions:
- Tokens/sec sizing: given avg 300 tokens/request, steady tokens/sec = 200 * 300 = ~60k tokens/sec. Peak tokens/sec = 1,200 * 300 = ~360k tokens/sec.
- GPU counts: initial estimate (conservative) — with int8 quantized model and our runtime optimizations, expect ~1 A100-80GB-equivalent can sustain ~50k tokens/sec for chat-style generation (depends on model family). So steady state ~1–2 GPUs; peak bursts would require ~7–8 GPUs if fully unbatched. We recommend autoscaling + burst capacity rather than sizing for sustained peak.
- Concurrency/streaming: streaming increases tail latency sensitivity; our continuous-batching + prefix KV cache reduces per-token work for multi-turn chats. For token-level streaming with P99 <= 800ms we typically set a small max-batch window (5–10ms) on the critical route and allow larger batching on non-streaming/async endpoints.
- Latency SLO tradeoffs: to hit P50/P95 targets while batching, we use priority routing (low-latency pool) for interactive sessions and a cheaper, higher-batch pool for background jobs.

Clarifying Qs so we size closer:
1) For the peak bursts, what is the typical burst duration (you mentioned 5–10 mins in the call — confirm).
2) Of requests, what % require streaming token-by-token vs a single aggregated response? (helps split low-latency pool sizing).
3) Do you plan to use the largest models in our catalog or a distilled/quantized variant? If you can share the model family we can give tighter GPU counts.

I can produce a short sizing worksheet that translates your traffic into Redwood pools (low-latency streaming pool, background pool, and caching layer). I’ll also include an estimate for hosted vs dedicated pricing for the two configurations.

Next steps: I’ll draft the sizing sheet and send it by EOD tomorrow. Can we schedule a 30‑minute follow-up on Fri to review?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-initial-suggested-config.pdf (doc stub)
